query: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization but a low coercive field, and reported single-phase fcc high-entropy alloys derived from it have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe in the reported magnetic measurements. What single intervention could overcome this coercivity limitation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted change relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative, the relevant compositional, structural, and measurement boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Introduction of grain boundaries through nanostructuring can increase the coercive field of single-phase fcc FeCoNi high-entropy alloys.
generation.mechanism: Pinning of domain walls at grain boundaries
generation.predicted_outcome: Increase in coercive field by a factor of 2-5 relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi
generation.baseline: Coercive field of single-phase fcc FeCoNi high-entropy alloy (<= 100 Oe)
generation.boundary: Grain size, composition (limited to FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloys)
generation.uncertainty: Magnitude of coercive field increase, optimal grain size

falsification_experiment.design: Compare coercive fields of nanostructured and single-phase fcc FeCoNi high-entropy alloy samples
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coercive field of the nanostructured sample is not significantly higher than that of the single-phase sample, the hypothesis is falsified.
